Health behaviours and wellbeing (simulated)

wellbeing.Rd

Six continuous health-behaviour and wellbeing indicators of 1,000 adults, designed for latent profile analysis (lpa()) with every variance/covariance structure and the bootstrap likelihood-ratio test (blrt()).

Usage

wellbeing

Format

A data frame with 1,000 rows and 10 columns:

id

Respondent id.

sleep

Hours of sleep per night.

activity

Hours of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week.

fruitveg

Servings of fruit and vegetables per day.

stress

Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-4), 0–16.

lonely

UCLA 3-item loneliness scale, 3–9.

lifesat

Life satisfaction, 0–10.

female

1 = woman.

age

Age in years, 18–79.

low_income

Low household income (0/1).

Indicators are rounded to one decimal and each is missing completely at random with probability 0.02.

Source

Simulated by datasets/generate.jl of LatentMixtures.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261102)); codebook in its datasets/README.md. Four profiles: Thriving (sample share 0.237; means sleep 7.6, activity 6.0, fruitveg 4.6, stress 3.5, lonely 3.6, lifesat 8.3), Typical (0.436; 7.1, 3.5, 3.1, 6.0, 4.6, 7.1), Stressed short sleepers (0.232; 5.9, 2.8, 2.4, 11.0, 6.0, 5.2) and Isolated and inactive (0.095; 8.0, 0.9, 1.9, 8.5, 7.8, 4.6), with profile-specific standard deviations and a common within-profile correlation matrix (stress–life satisfaction -0.35, sleep–stress -0.25, loneliness–life satisfaction -0.30, stress–loneliness 0.25, activity–diet 0.20). Profile membership depends on low_income, female and age. Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Examples

data(wellbeing)
summary(wellbeing[, c("sleep", "activity", "stress", "lifesat")])
#>      sleep           activity          stress          lifesat      
#>  Min.   : 3.400   Min.   : 0.000   Min.   : 0.000   Min.   : 0.900  
#>  1st Qu.: 6.500   1st Qu.: 2.200   1st Qu.: 4.200   1st Qu.: 5.700  
#>  Median : 7.150   Median : 3.600   Median : 6.200   Median : 6.900  
#>  Mean   : 7.044   Mean   : 3.718   Mean   : 6.674   Mean   : 6.698  
#>  3rd Qu.: 7.700   3rd Qu.: 4.900   3rd Qu.: 9.000   3rd Qu.: 7.900  
#>  Max.   :10.200   Max.   :12.700   Max.   :16.000   Max.   :10.000  
#>  NAs    :14       NAs    :25       NAs    :15       NAs    :17      
# \donttest{
# are there distinct wellbeing profiles? four profiles, profile-specific variances
p <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying")
#> Starting Julia ...
profilemeans(p)  # e.g. a short-sleeping, highly stressed profile
#>            class1   class2    class3    class4
#> sleep    7.085464 7.600044  5.877936 7.8894882
#> activity 3.541653 5.780687  2.839283 0.9176709
#> fruitveg 2.973951 4.385015  2.428910 1.9636675
#> stress   6.089048 3.291932 11.097546 8.6762339
#> lonely   4.598344 3.700244  6.049324 7.6170787
#> lifesat  6.992607 8.256812  5.192539 4.6306269
# }
